OpsBot: INCIDENT: gpu-pool-deg detected in asia-south3 (capacity below 40% util for high-priority queues). Auto-remediation attempted: scaled +0 replicas (quota hit).

Maya P.: Seeing increased queue latency for chat-inference in asia-south3, getting OOM errors on a few pods. Paging infra oncall.

Chen L.: Acknowledge. Checking GPU pool quotas and node health now.

Samir R.: Logs show node evictions around 03:12 UTC, nv_peer_mem errors + network flaps between rack-12 and infra fabric.

Priya N.: Can we shift traffic to us-west2 dedicated pool while we investigate? Need to avoid customer impact.

Maya P.: Yes — plan: 1) set routing override to prefer us-west2 for chat-inference for next 30m 2) open dedicated burst on us-west2 3) attempt graceful drain of affected nodes.

Leo C.: I can apply routing override. Will also throttle non-PLG burst to reduce cost.

Chen L.: Running quick health commands:
```
# check node statuses
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-asia-south3 -o wide
# inspect recent evictions
kubectl describe pod <example-pod> -n prod-chat
```

Samir R.: Confirmed 6 nodes in NotReady state, kernel taints from NIC driver. Suggest rolling driver restart after draining.

Maya P.: Doing manual drain on 6 nodes now. Marking them unschedulable. Will coordinate with infra for driver restart.

OpsBot: RUNBOOK STEP: If >5 nodes degraded -> open regional failover (routing override) and notify SRE lead.

Priya N.: Applied routing override: traffic now Rerouted -> us-west2 (10:56 UTC). Observability shows p50 latencies back to normal for high-priority jobs.

Leo C.: Enabled burst capacity on us-west2: +8 GPUs (temporary). Cost note: estimated incremental $1.2k/hr if sustained.

Chen L.: Infra team queued a maintenance window for driver restarts. ETA 20 minutes.

Samir R.: After driver restart, we should re-evaluate kernel logs and perform a controlled uncordon.

Maya P.: Paging policy tweak proposal: for this class of NIC flaps in a single region, reduce immediate P1 paging to on-call only when degraded pool impacts >20% of capacity AND auto-remediation fails. Otherwise send channel alert only. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Priya N.: Agrees. We get a lot of noisy pages for transient fabric blips. Lowering noise will help response quality during real infra events.

Leo C.: +1. Suggestation: add a 3-minute aggregation window and require 2 distinct eviction signals before a P1 page.

Chen L.: I'll open a PR to adjust pagerbot rules: add aggregation window + sample count and a fallback to immediate page for customer-facing SLA breaches.

OpsBot: ACTION CREATED: pagerbot/pr-452 for 'region-nic-eviction-aggregation' by Chen L.

Maya P.: Handoff note for next oncall (in 40m): keep routing override for 30m unless pool stability confirmed, coordinate with infra for full cluster health checks, and verify no regression in cache hit rates after reroute.

Samir R.: Postmortem checklist item: analyze kernel logs across affected nodes, vendor NIC firmware compatibility, and whether autoscaler should treat NIC flaps as transient vs node-fail.

Priya N.: Current status: us-west2 serving steady, asia-south3 at 60% capacity after restarts, draining complete. Will update channel when all nodes uncordoned.

Leo C.: Uncordoned one node for smoke — looks healthy. Will slowly bring others back.

Maya P.: Thanks all. Good containment. Will draft incident summary and include cost impact, pagerbot tweak request, and follow-ups.

Priya N.: Closing thread for now, will ping once asia-south3 is fully healthy. :white_check_mark:
